subject: Concurrency & token-split governance for dedicated capacity — follow-up
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <mike@hearthly.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + sizing asks from today's call

Hi Mike — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can firm up a dedicated capacity proposal.

Recap (high level)
- Your preference: Dedicated capacity (private tenant) with VPC peering and SOC 2 evidence.
- Primary workload: customer-facing summarization + retrieval-augmented generation for support and billing flows.
- Target go-live: early Q3 (pilot), full rollout by Q4.

Sizing / qualification asks (short list) — would appreciate answers by EOD Tue:
1) Target steady-state TPS (inference requests/sec) and expected burst TPS.
2) Average tokens/request (input + output). Percentile breakdown (p50/p95) if possible.
3) Typical concurrency pattern (many small concurrent requests vs fewer long-running ones).
4) Any hard latency SLOs (p95 end-to-end generation latency).
5) Do you have a GPU preference (H100 vs A100) from procurement? Any procurement constraints.
6) VPC/on-prem requirement confirmation and any egress restrictions.

Attachments: I dropped a short template for token profile we discussed — fill that out and attach. Also linking our dedicated SKU overview PDF in case procurement asks.

Next steps
- We’ll run a quick sizing pass with the numbers you provide and propose 2 SKU options (throughput-optimized vs cost-optimized).
- Workshop: 60 minutes with Karthik and Ben to finalize concurrency + batch policies.

Thanks —
Tessa
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

---

From: Mike Chen <mike@hearthly.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@hearthly.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2027 10:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + sizing asks from today's call

Tessa — great summary, appreciate it. Answers inline below and I attached the token profile CSV as requested.

1) Steady-state TPS: ~100 requests/sec (this is what we expect after pilot). Burst: up to ~400 rps for short windows (1–3 minutes) during end-of-month billing runs.
2) Average tokens/request: ~900 tokens (input + output). p50 ~700, p95 ~1,600. We have a small number (~2%) of very large multimodal jobs that spike to 6k tokens but those are off the critical path.
3) Concurrency: simultaneous short requests — typically 50–120 concurrent short generations. We don’t queue on the client side; we prefer low tail latency.
4) Latency SLO: p95 generation under 800ms for the majority (customer-facing flows). Billing workflows can tolerate 2–3s for the rare long jobs.
5) GPU preference: procurement prefers A100 for cost reasons but engineering prefers H100 for headroom. Procurement asked for a detailed comparison/cost delta.
6) VPC: yes, must be VPC peering with strict egress rules (no public internet access from inference hosts). SOC 2 is required; we’ll need audit artifacts.

Timeline: pilot kick-off week of Jul 12, pilot duration 4 weeks, then decision.

Thanks —
Mike
Head of Product — Hearthly

Attachment: hearthly_token_profile.csv

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <mike@hearthly.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2027 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up + sizing asks from today's call

Mike — thanks for the quick data, that helps a lot. A few technical notes based on the profile you shared:

- H100 vs A100: for steady 100 TPS with p95 latency target ~800ms and p95 tokens ~1.6k, H100 gives better headroom especially if you want to avoid aggressive quantization. A100 + int8/4-bit quantization can be significantly cheaper but will require validation on your prompt quality and an acceptance test set.
- Burst handling: to safely cover 400 rps bursts we recommend a combination of a modest buffer (burst pool) plus autoscale thresholds and an emergency fallback to a lower-cost model variant.
- Batching & KV cache: with your token mix, continuous batching (short windows, e.g., 5–10ms) plus KV cache for recent contexts should reduce per-token cost without breaking latency SLOs.
- Concurrency note: 50–120 concurrent short requests with ~900 tokens average maps to ~45–90 GPU contexts if we avoid aggressive horizontal sharding. We’ll size pools accordingly.

Requests for the sizing workshop
1) Can you confirm p99 token length for the billing job spikes?
2) Are the 6k-token multimodal jobs going to be run against the same endpoints or isolated to a different pipeline?
3) Any encryption/KMS preferences for the VPC deployment?

I’ll draft two SKU options (H100 throughput-optimized, A100 cost-optimized) and include expected p95 latency and unit cost. Ben — can you drop a ballpark monthly commit for each SKU so procurement has a starting point?

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

- A100 cost SKU (pilot): $29k/month — with quantization and validation phase to meet latency targets; less headroom on headroom for worst-case tails.

Notes:

- Pricing above is pilot-level; annual reserved discounts available if you commit to a 12+ month Dedicated contract.
